description:
FILED s510b (Opus, 2026-10-07); perl 5.40.3.
  open(my $p, '-|', "printf 'a\\n\\303\\251\\n'"); my $l1 = <$p>; binmode($p, ':utf8'); my $l2 = <$p>;
  perl: $l2 = "\x{e9}\n"     PCL: undef (before s510b too: the old rebuild lost it the same way)
A seekable handle is right since s510b (the logical position is saved and re-sought).  A descriptor that cannot seek has its bytes in SBCL's ibuf and decoded characters in the ansi-stream cin-buffer; set-fd-stream-routines resets the ibuf.  Direction: before the re-install, take the unconsumed bytes (ibuf head..tail) plus the unconsumed decoded characters re-encoded in the OLD format, and put them back into the reset ibuf.  Measure first whether the cin-buffer survives (buffer-p NIL keeps the array; its in-index is not reset).  Documented in not-supported.md (layer section).
subject: binmode on a PARTLY-READ pipe / socket loses the read-ahead (perl re-decodes it under the new layer)
